# Skill: better-auth-security-best-practices

## Secret Management

### Configuring the Secret

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  secret: process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, // or via `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` env
});
```

Better Auth looks for secrets in this order:
1. `options.secret` in your config
2. `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` environment variable
3. `AUTH_SECRET` environment variable

### Secret Requirements

- Rejects default/placeholder secrets in production
- Warns if shorter than 32 characters or entropy below 120 bits
- Generate: `openssl rand -base64 32`
- Never commit secrets to version control

## Rate Limiting

Enabled in production by default. Applies to all endpoints. Plugins can override per-endpoint.

### Default Configuration

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  rateLimit: {
    enabled: true, // Default: true in production
    window: 10, // Time window in seconds (default: 10)
    max: 100, // Max requests per window (default: 100)
  },
});
```

### Storage Options

Options: `"memory"` (resets on restart, avoid on serverless), `"database"` (persistent), `"secondary-storage"` (Redis, default when available).

```ts
rateLimit: {
  storage: "database",
}
```

### Custom Storage

Implement your own rate limit storage:

```ts
rateLimit: {
  customStorage: {
    get: async (key) => {
      // Return { count: number, expiresAt: number } or null
    },
    set: async (key, data) => {
      // Store the rate limit data
    },
  },
}
```

### Per-Endpoint Rules

Sensitive endpoints default to 3 requests per 10 seconds (`/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/change-password`, `/change-email`). Override:

```ts
rateLimit: {
  customRules: {
    "/api/auth/sign-in/email": {
      window: 60, // 1 minute window
      max: 5, // 5 attempts
    },
    "/api/auth/some-safe-endpoint": false, // Disable rate limiting
  },
}
```

## CSRF Protection

Multi-layer protection: origin header validation, Fetch Metadata checks, and first-login protection.

### Configuration

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  advanced: {
    disableCSRFCheck: false, // Default: false (keep enabled)
  },
});
```

Only disable for testing or with an alternative CSRF mechanism.

## Trusted Origins

### Configuring Trusted Origins

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  baseURL: "https://api.example.com",
  trustedOrigins: [
    "https://app.example.com",
    "https://admin.example.com",
  ],
});
```

The `baseURL` origin is automatically trusted. Also configurable via env: `BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://app.example.com,https://admin.example.com`

### Wildcard Patterns

```ts
trustedOrigins: [
  "*.example.com", // Matches any subdomain
  "https://*.example.com", // Protocol-specific wildcard
  "exp://192.168.*.*:*/*", // Custom schemes (e.g., Expo)
]
```

### Dynamic Trusted Origins

Compute trusted origins based on the request:

```ts
trustedOrigins: async (request) => {
  // Validate against database, header, etc.
  const tenant = getTenantFromRequest(request);
  return [`https://${tenant}.myapp.com`];
}
```

Validates `callbackURL`, `redirectTo`, `errorCallbackURL`, `newUserCallbackURL`, and `origin` against trusted origins. Invalid URLs receive 403.

## Session Security

### Session Expiration

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  session: {
    expiresIn: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7, // 7 days (default)
    updateAge: 60 * 60 * 24, // Refresh session every 24 hours (default)
  },
});
```

### Session Caching Strategies

Cache session data in cookies to reduce database queries:

```ts
session: {
  cookieCache: {
    enabled: true,
    maxAge: 60 * 5, // 5 minutes
    strategy: "compact", // Options: "compact", "jwt", "jwe"
  },
}
```

Strategies: `"compact"` (Base64url + HMAC, smallest), `"jwt"` (HS256, standard), `"jwe"` (encrypted, use when session has sensitive data).

## Cookie Security

Defaults: `secure: true` (HTTPS/production), `sameSite: "lax"`, `httpOnly: true`, `path: "/"`, prefix `__Secure-`.

### Custom Cookie Configuration

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  advanced: {
    useSecureCookies: true, // Force secure cookies
    cookiePrefix: "myapp", // Custom prefix (default: "better-auth")
    defaultCookieAttributes: {
      sameSite: "strict", // Stricter CSRF protection
      path: "/auth", // Limit cookie scope
    },
  },
});
```

### Cross-Subdomain Cookies

```ts
advanced: {
  crossSubDomainCookies: {
    enabled: true,
    domain: ".example.com", // Note the leading dot
    additionalCookies: ["session_token", "session_data"],
  },
}
```

Only enable if you need authentication sharing and trust all subdomains.

## OAuth / Social Provider Security

PKCE is automatic for all OAuth flows. State tokens are 32-char random strings expiring after 10 minutes.

### State Parameter Storage

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  account: {
    storeStateStrategy: "cookie", // Options: "cookie" (default), "database"
  },
});
```

### Encrypting OAuth Tokens

```ts
account: {
  encryptOAuthTokens: true, // Uses AES-256-GCM
}
```

Enable if storing OAuth tokens for API access on behalf of users. Use `skipStateCookieCheck: true` only for mobile apps that cannot maintain cookies.

## IP-Based Security

### IP Address Configuration

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  advanced: {
    ipAddress: {
      ipAddressHeaders: ["x-forwarded-for", "x-real-ip"], // Headers to check
      disableIpTracking: false, // Keep enabled for rate limiting
    },
  },
});
```

Set `ipv6Subnet` (128, 64, 48, 32; default 64) to group IPv6 addresses. Enable `trustedProxyHeaders: true` only if behind a trusted reverse proxy.

## Database Hooks for Security Auditing

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  databaseHooks: {
    session: {
      create: {
        after: async ({ data, ctx }) => {
          await auditLog("session.created", {
            userId: data.userId,
            ip: ctx?.request?.headers.get("x-forwarded-for"),
            userAgent: ctx?.request?.headers.get("user-agent"),
          });
        },
      },
      delete: {
        before: async ({ data }) => {
          await auditLog("session.revoked", { sessionId: data.id });
        },
      },
    },
    user: {
      update: {
        after: async ({ data, oldData }) => {
          if (oldData?.email !== data.email) {
            await auditLog("user.email_changed", {
              userId: data.id,
              oldEmail: oldData?.email,
              newEmail: data.email,
            });
          }
        },
      },
    },
    account: {
      create: {
        after: async ({ data }) => {
          await auditLog("account.linked", {
            userId: data.userId,
            provider: data.providerId,
          });
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

Return `false` from a `before` hook to prevent an operation.

## Background Tasks

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  advanced: {
    backgroundTasks: {
      handler: (promise) => {
        // Platform-specific handler
        // Vercel: waitUntil(promise)
        // Cloudflare: ctx.waitUntil(promise)
        waitUntil(promise);
      },
    },
  },
});
```

Ensures operations like sending emails don't affect response timing.

## Account Enumeration Prevention

Built-in: consistent response messages, dummy operations on invalid requests, background email sending. Return generic error messages ("Invalid credentials") rather than specific ones ("User not found").

## Complete Security Configuration Example

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  secret: process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET,
  baseURL: "https://api.example.com",
  trustedOrigins: [
    "https://app.example.com",
    "https://*.preview.example.com",
  ],
  
  // Rate limiting
  rateLimit: {
    enabled: true,
    storage: "secondary-storage",
    customRules: {
      "/api/auth/sign-in/email": { window: 60, max: 5 },
      "/api/auth/sign-up/email": { window: 60, max: 3 },
    },
  },
  
  // Session security
  session: {
    expiresIn: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7, // 7 days
    updateAge: 60 * 60 * 24, // 24 hours
    freshAge: 60 * 60, // 1 hour for sensitive actions
    cookieCache: {
      enabled: true,
      maxAge: 300,
      strategy: "jwe", // Encrypted session data
    },
  },
  
  // OAuth security
  account: {
    encryptOAuthTokens: true,
    storeStateStrategy: "cookie",
  },
  
  
  // Advanced settings
  advanced: {
    useSecureCookies: true,
    cookiePrefix: "myapp",
    defaultCookieAttributes: {
      sameSite: "lax",
    },
    ipAddress: {
      ipAddressHeaders: ["x-forwarded-for"],
      ipv6Subnet: 64,
    },
    backgroundTasks: {
      handler: (promise) => waitUntil(promise),
    },
  },
  
  // Security auditing
  databaseHooks: {
    session: {
      create: {
        after: async ({ data, ctx }) => {
          console.log(`New session for user ${data.userId}`);
        },
      },
    },
    user: {
      update: {
        after: async ({ data, oldData }) => {
          if (oldData?.email !== data.email) {
            console.log(`Email changed for user ${data.id}`);
          }
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

## Security Checklist

Before deploying to production:

- [ ] **Secret**: Use a strong, unique secret (32+ characters, high entropy)
- [ ] **HTTPS**: Ensure `baseURL` uses HTTPS
- [ ] **Trusted Origins**: Configure all valid origins (frontend, mobile apps)
- [ ] **Rate Limiting**: Keep enabled with appropriate limits
- [ ] **CSRF Protection**: Keep enabled (`disableCSRFCheck: false`)
- [ ] **Secure Cookies**: Enabled automatically with HTTPS
- [ ] **OAuth Tokens**: Consider `encryptOAuthTokens: true` if storing tokens
- [ ] **Background Tasks**: Configure for serverless platforms
- [ ] **Audit Logging**: Implement via `databaseHooks` or `hooks`
- [ ] **IP Tracking**: Configure headers if behind a proxy

219:        ON CONFLICT(bucket_key) DO UPDATE SET
220:          count = CASE
221:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN 1
222:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.count + 1
223:          END,
224:          window_started_at = CASE
225:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN ?
226:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at
227:          END,
228:          updated_at = ?
229:        RETURNING count, window_started_at`,
230:     )
231:     .bind(key, now, now, windowMilliseconds, now, windowMilliseconds, now, now, now)
232:     .first<{ count: number; window_started_at: number }>();
233: 
234:   if (!bucket) throw new M1Error(500);
235: 
236:   if (bucket.count === 1) {
237:     const db = createDb(database);
238:     await db
239:       .delete(rateLimitBuckets)
240:       .where(lt(rateLimitBuckets.updatedAt, now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000))
241:       .run();
242:   }
243: 
244:   return bucket.count <= max;
245: }

465: async function ensureControlledUser(
466:   auth: AuthInstance,
467:   email: string,
468:   name: string,
469:   password: string,
470:   existingUserId?: string | null,
471:   allowExistingCredential = false,
472:   existingSince?: number | null,
473: ): Promise<ManagedUser> {
474:   const context = await auth.$context;
475:   let user = existingUserId ? await context.internalAdapter.findUserById(existingUserId) : null;
476: 
477:   if (!user) {
478:     const existing = await context.internalAdapter.findUserByEmail(email, {
479:       includeAccounts: true,
480:     });
481:     user = existing?.user ?? null;
482:     if (
483:       user &&
484:       !allowExistingCredential &&
485:       existing?.accounts.some((account) => account.providerId === "credential")
486:     ) {
487:       const createdAt = new Date(user.createdAt).getTime();
488:       if (!existingSince || createdAt < existingSince) throw new M1Error(409);
489:     }
490:   }
491:   if (user && normalizeEmail(user.email) !== email) throw new M1Error(409);
492: 
493:   if (!user) {
494:     const passwordHash = await context.password.hash(password);
495:     try {
496:       user = await context.internalAdapter.createUser(
497:         { email, emailVerified: false, name },
498:         { method: "email-password" },
499:       );
500:     } catch {
501:       user =
502:         (await context.internalAdapter.findUserByEmail(email, { includeAccounts: true }))?.user ??
503:         null;
504:       if (!user) throw new M1Error(500);
505:     }
506: 
507:     try {
508:       await context.internalAdapter.linkAccount({
509:         accountId: user.id,
510:         issuer: createLocalAccountIssuer("credential"),
511:         password: passwordHash,
512:         providerId: "credential",
513:         userId: user.id,
514:       });
515:     } catch {
516:       if (!(await context.internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount(user.id))) throw new M1Error(500);
517:     }
518:   } else {
519:     const credential = await context.internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount(user.id);
520:     if (!credential) {
521:       const passwordHash = await context.password.hash(password);
522:       try {
523:         await context.internalAdapter.linkAccount({
524:           accountId: user.id,
525:           issuer: createLocalAccountIssuer("credential"),
526:           password: passwordHash,
527:           providerId: "credential",
528:           userId: user.id,
529:         });
530:       } catch {
531:         if (!(await context.internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount(user.id))) throw new M1Error(500);
532:       }
533:     } else if (allowExistingCredential) {
534:       const passwordHash = await context.password.hash(password);
535:       await context.internalAdapter.updatePassword(user.id, passwordHash);
536:     }
537:   }
538: 
539:   return user as ManagedUser;
540: }

595:   database: D1Database,

602:   if (existingMapping && existingMapping.id !== principalId) throw new M1Error(409);

605:     (existingMapping.type !== "human" ||
606:       (!allowDisabled &&
607:         (existingMapping.principal_status !== "active" ||
608:           existingMapping.human_status !== "active" ||
609:           existingMapping.disabled !== 0)))

611:     throw new M1Error(409);

614:   const existingPrincipal = await createDb(database)

616:     .from(principals)
617:     .where(eq(principals.id, principalId))
618:     .get();
619:   if (
620:     existingPrincipal &&
621:     (existingPrincipal.type !== "human" ||
622:       (!allowDisabled && existingPrincipal.status !== "active"))
623:   ) {
624:     throw new M1Error(409);
625:   }
626: 
627:   const db = createDb(database);
628:   await db.batch([
629:     db
630:       .insert(principals)
631:       .values({
632:         id: principalId,
633:         type: "human",
634:         status: "active",
635:         disabledAt: null,
636:         createdAt: now,
637:         updatedAt: now,
638:       })
639:       .onConflictDoUpdate({
640:         target: principals.id,
641:         set: { disabledAt: null, status: "active", updatedAt: now },
642:       }),
643:     db
644:       .insert(humanPrincipals)
645:       .values({
646:         principalId,
647:         userId,
648:         status: "active",
649:         disabled: false,
650:         disabledAt: null,
651:         createdAt: now,
652:         updatedAt: now,
653:       })
654:       .onConflictDoUpdate({
655:         target: humanPrincipals.principalId,
656:         set: { disabled: false, disabledAt: null, status: "active", userId, updatedAt: now },
657:       }),
658:   ]);
659: 
660:   const mapping = await readHumanMapping(database, userId);
661:   if (
662:     !mapping ||
663:     mapping.id !== principalId ||
664:     mapping.principal_status !== "active" ||
665:     mapping.human_status !== "active" ||
666:     mapping.disabled !== 0
667:   ) {
668:     throw new M1Error(500);

671:   return principalId;

765: async function completeBootstrapDomain(
766:   database: D1Database,
767:   state: BootstrapState,
768:   user: ManagedUser,
769:   principalId: string,
770:   now: number,
771: ) {
772:   const existingRoot = await createDb(database)
773:     .select({ principalId: systemRoleGrants.principalId })
774:     .from(systemRoleGrants)
775:     .innerJoin(systemRoles, eq(systemRoles.id, systemRoleGrants.roleId))
776:     .innerJoin(principals, eq(principals.id, systemRoleGrants.principalId))
777:     .innerJoin(humanPrincipals, eq(humanPrincipals.principalId, principals.id))
778:     .where(
779:       and(
780:         eq(systemRoles.key, "root"),
781:         isNull(systemRoleGrants.revokedAt),
782:         eq(principals.type, "human"),
783:         eq(principals.status, "active"),
784:         eq(humanPrincipals.status, "active"),
785:         eq(humanPrincipals.disabled, false),
786:       ),
787:     )
788:     .get();
789:   if (existingRoot && existingRoot.principalId !== principalId) throw new M1Error(409);
790: 
791:   const email = state.email ?? normalizeEmail(user.email);
792:   const eventId = `bootstrap:completed:${state.reservation_id ?? principalId}`;
793:   const results = await database.batch([
794:     database
795:       .prepare(
796:         `UPDATE bootstrap_state
797:             SET status = 'completed', principal_id = ?, completed_at = ?, updated_at = ?
798:           WHERE id = 1
799:             AND status IN ('reserved', 'user-created')
800:             AND reservation_id = ?
801:             AND email = ?
802:             AND user_id = ?
803:           RETURNING id`,
804:       )
805:       .bind(principalId, now, now, state.reservation_id, email, user.id),
806:     grantBootstrapRoleStatement(database, state.reservation_id ?? "", user.id, principalId, now),
807:     auditStatementWhen(
808:       database,
809:       eventId,
810:       "bootstrap.completed",
811:       null,
812:       principalId,
813:       user.id,
814:       { email },
815:       now,
816:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'completed' AND reservation_id = ? AND user_id = ?",
817:       [state.reservation_id, user.id],
818:     ),
819:     outboxStatementWhen(
820:       database,
821:       `bootstrap:completed:outbox:${state.reservation_id ?? principalId}`,
822:       "bootstrap.completed",
823:       "bootstrap",
824:       "1",
825:       { principalId, userId: user.id },
826:       now,
827:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'completed' AND reservation_id = ? AND user_id = ?",
828:       [state.reservation_id, user.id],
829:     ),
830:   ]);
831:   if (!results[0]?.results.length) throw new M1Error(409);
832: }

834: async function reserveBootstrap(
835:   environment: AuthEnvironment,
836:   body: BootstrapTokenBody,
837:   request: Request,
838: ) {
839:   await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "bootstrap-reserve", 50, 60);
840:   await requireBootstrapToken(environment, body);
841:   const state = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
842:   if (state.status === "completed") throw new M1Error(404);
843:   if (state.status !== "uninitialized") {
844:     if (!state.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(500);
845:     return { reservationId: state.reservation_id, status: state.status };
846:   }
847: 
848:   const reservationId = crypto.randomUUID();
849:   const now = Date.now();
850:   const results = await environment.DB.batch([
851:     environment.DB.prepare(
852:       `UPDATE bootstrap_state
853:               SET status = 'reserved', reservation_id = ?, reserved_at = ?, updated_at = ?
854:             WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'uninitialized'
855:             RETURNING reservation_id, status`,
856:     ).bind(reservationId, now, now),
857:     auditStatementWhen(
858:       environment.DB,
859:       `bootstrap:reserved:${reservationId}`,
860:       "bootstrap.reserved",
861:       null,
862:       null,
863:       null,
864:       {},
865:       now,
866:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'reserved' AND reservation_id = ? AND reserved_at = ?",
867:       [reservationId, now],
868:     ),
869:     outboxStatementWhen(
870:       environment.DB,
871:       `bootstrap:reserved:outbox:${reservationId}`,
872:       "bootstrap.reserved",
873:       "bootstrap",
874:       "1",
875:       { reservationId },
876:       now,
877:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'reserved' AND reservation_id = ? AND reserved_at = ?",
878:       [reservationId, now],
879:     ),
880:   ]);
881:   const reserved = results[0]?.results[0] as
882:     | { reservation_id: string; status: BootstrapStatus }
883:     | undefined;
884: 
885:   if (!reserved) {
886:     const racedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
887:     if (racedState.status === "completed" || !racedState.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(409);
888:     return { reservationId: racedState.reservation_id, status: racedState.status };
889:   }
890: 
891:   return { reservationId, status: reserved.status };
892: }

898:   request: Request,
899: ) {
900:   await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "bootstrap-complete", 50, 60);
901:   await requireBootstrapToken(environment, body);
902:   const state = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
903:   if (state.status === "completed") {
904:     if (state.email && normalizeEmail(body.email) !== state.email) throw new M1Error(409);
905:     return { status: state.status, userId: state.user_id };
906:   }
907:   if (state.status === "uninitialized" || !state.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(409);
908:   if (body.reservationId && body.reservationId !== state.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(409);
909: 
910:   const email = normalizeEmail(body.email);
911:   if (state.email && state.email !== email) throw new M1Error(409);
912: 
913:   const context = await auth.$context;
914:   if (
915:     body.password.length < context.password.config.minPasswordLength ||
916:     body.password.length > context.password.config.maxPasswordLength
917:   ) {
918:     throw new M1Error(400);
919:   }
920: 
921:   if (!state.email) {
922:     const claimedEmail = await environment.DB.prepare(
923:       `UPDATE bootstrap_state
924:             SET email = ?, updated_at = ?
925:           WHERE id = 1
926:             AND status = 'reserved'
927:             AND reservation_id = ?
928:             AND (email IS NULL OR email = ?)
929:           RETURNING email`,
930:     )
931:       .bind(email, Date.now(), state.reservation_id, email)
932:       .first<{ email: string }>();
933:     if (!claimedEmail) {
934:       const racedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
935:       if (racedState.email !== email) throw new M1Error(409);
936:     }
937:   }
938: 
939:   const user = await ensureControlledUser(
940:     auth,
941:     email,
942:     normalizeName(body.name, email),
943:     body.password,
944:     state.user_id,
945:     false,
946:     state.reserved_at,
947:   );
948:   const marked = await environment.DB.prepare(
949:     `UPDATE bootstrap_state
950:           SET status = 'user-created', user_id = ?, user_created_at = COALESCE(user_created_at, ?), updated_at = ?
951:         WHERE id = 1
952:           AND status IN ('reserved', 'user-created')
953:           AND reservation_id = ?
954:           AND email = ?
955:           AND (user_id IS NULL OR user_id = ?)
956:         RETURNING user_id`,
957:   )
958:     .bind(user.id, Date.now(), Date.now(), state.reservation_id, email, user.id)
959:     .first<{ user_id: string }>();
960:   if (!marked) {
961:     const racedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
962:     if (racedState.user_id !== user.id) throw new M1Error(409);
963:   }
964: 
965:   const markedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
966:   await sendVerificationEmail(auth, user);
967:   const principalId = await ensureHumanPrincipal(environment.DB, user.id, Date.now());
968:   await completeBootstrapDomain(environment.DB, markedState, user, principalId, Date.now());
969: 
970:   return { principalId, status: "completed" as const, userId: user.id };
971: }

997: async function expireInvitation(
998:   database: D1Database,
999:   invitation: Pick<Invitation, "id">,
1000:   now: number,
1001:   force = false,
1002: ) {
1003:   const principalSubquery = `
1004:     SELECT COALESCE(claimed_principal_id, 'human_' || claimed_user_id)
1005:       FROM invitations
1006:      WHERE id = ? AND status = 'expired' AND claimed_user_id IS NOT NULL
1007:        AND (? = 1 OR expired_at = ?)`;
1008:   await database.batch([
1009:     database
1010:       .prepare(
1011:         `UPDATE invitations
1012:           SET status = 'expired', expired_at = ?, updated_at = ?
1013:         WHERE id = ?
1014:           AND expired_at IS NULL
1015:           AND ((status IN ('pending', 'claimed') AND expires_at <= ?) OR status = 'expired')`,
1016:       )
1017:       .bind(now, now, invitation.id, now),
1018:     database
1019:       .prepare(
1020:         `UPDATE human_principals
1021:           SET status = 'disabled', disabled = 1, disabled_at = ?, updated_at = ?
1022:         WHERE principal_id = (${principalSubquery})`,
1023:       )
1024:       .bind(now, now, invitation.id, force ? 1 : 0, now),
1025:     database
1026:       .prepare(
1027:         `UPDATE principals
1028:           SET status = 'disabled', disabled_at = ?, updated_at = ?
1029:         WHERE id = (${principalSubquery}) AND status = 'active'`,
1030:       )
1031:       .bind(now, now, invitation.id, force ? 1 : 0, now),
1032:     database
1033:       .prepare(
1034:         `DELETE FROM session
1035:         WHERE user_id = (
1036:           SELECT claimed_user_id
1037:             FROM invitations
1038:            WHERE id = ? AND status = 'expired' AND claimed_user_id IS NOT NULL
1039:              AND (? = 1 OR expired_at = ?)
1040:          )`,
1041:       )
1042:       .bind(invitation.id, force ? 1 : 0, now),
1043:     database
1044:       .prepare(
1045:         `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO audit_events
1046:          (id, event_type, actor_principal_id, subject_principal_id, subject_user_id, metadata, created_at)
1047:          SELECT ?, 'invitation.expired', NULL,
1048:                 (SELECT id FROM principals WHERE id = COALESCE(i.claimed_principal_id, 'human_' || i.claimed_user_id)),
1049:                 i.claimed_user_id, ?, ?
1050:            FROM invitations AS i
1051:           WHERE i.id = ? AND i.status = 'expired' AND i.expired_at = ?`,
1052:       )
1053:       .bind(
1054:         `invitation:expired:${invitation.id}`,
1055:         JSON.stringify({ invitationId: invitation.id }),
1056:         now,
1057:         invitation.id,
1058:         now,
1059:       ),
1060:     database
1061:       .prepare(
1062:         `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO outbox_events
1063:          (id, dedupe_key, event_type, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, payload, status, attempts, available_at, created_at)
1064:          SELECT ?, ?, 'invitation.expired', 'invitation', ?, ?, 'pending', 0, ?, ?
1065:            FROM invitations AS i
1066:           WHERE i.id = ? AND i.status = 'expired' AND i.expired_at = ?`,
1067:       )
1068:       .bind(
1069:         `invitation:expired:${invitation.id}`,
1070:         `invitation:expired:outbox:${invitation.id}`,
1071:         invitation.id,
1072:         JSON.stringify({ invitationId: invitation.id }),
1073:         now,
1074:         now,
1075:         invitation.id,
1076:         now,
1077:       ),
1078:   ]);
1079: }

1098: async function createInvitation(
1099:   environment: AuthEnvironment,
1100:   actor: Actor,
1101:   body: InvitationCreateBody,
1102:   request: Request,
1103: ) {
1104:   await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "invitation-create", 30, 60);
1105:   const email = normalizeEmail(body.email);
1106:   const name = body.name ? normalizeName(body.name, email) : null;
1107:   const requestedRoleKeys = await validateRoleKeys(environment.DB, body.systemRoleKeys ?? []);
1108:   const now = Date.now();
1109:   const staleInvitations = await createDb(environment.DB)
1110:     .select({ expiresAt: invitations.expiresAt, id: invitations.id })
1111:     .from(invitations)
1112:     .where(
1113:       and(
1114:         eq(invitations.email, email),
1115:         inArray(invitations.status, ["pending", "claimed"]),
1116:         lte(invitations.expiresAt, now),
1117:       ),
1118:     )
1119:     .all();
1120:   for (const staleInvitation of staleInvitations) {
1121:     await expireInvitation(environment.DB, staleInvitation, now);
1122:   }
1123:   const existingMapping = await createDb(environment.DB)
1124:     .select({ userId: humanPrincipals.userId })
1125:     .from(humanPrincipals)
1126:     .innerJoin(principals, eq(principals.id, humanPrincipals.principalId))
1127:     .innerJoin(user, eq(user.id, humanPrincipals.userId))
1128:     .where(
1129:       and(
1130:         eq(user.email, email),
1131:         eq(principals.status, "active"),
1132:         eq(humanPrincipals.status, "active"),
1133:         eq(humanPrincipals.disabled, false),
1134:       ),
1135:     )
1136:     .get();
1137:   if (existingMapping) throw new M1Error(409);
1138:   const existingInvitation = await createDb(environment.DB)
1139:     .select({ id: invitations.id })
1140:     .from(invitations)
1141:     .where(and(eq(invitations.email, email), inArray(invitations.status, ["pending", "claimed"])))
1142:     .get();
1143:   if (existingInvitation) throw new M1Error(409);
1144: 
1145:   const token = randomToken();
1146:   const tokenHash = await sha256Base64Url(token);
1147:   const invitationId = crypto.randomUUID();
1148:   const requestedLifetime = body.expiresInSeconds ?? body.expiresIn ?? 60 * 60 * 24 * 7;
1149:   const expiresAt = now + requestedLifetime * 1000;
1150: 
1151:   try {
1152:     await environment.DB.batch([
1153:       environment.DB.prepare(
1154:         `INSERT INTO invitations
1155:             (id, token_hash, email, name, status, expires_at, invited_by_principal_id, system_role_keys, created_at, updated_at)
1156:            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'pending', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
1157:       ).bind(
1158:         invitationId,
1159:         tokenHash,
1160:         email,
1161:         name,
1162:         expiresAt,
1163:         actor.principalId,
1164:         JSON.stringify(requestedRoleKeys),
1165:         now,
1166:         now,
1167:       ),
1168:       auditStatement(
1169:         environment.DB,
1170:         `invitation:created:${invitationId}`,
1171:         "invitation.created",
1172:         actor.principalId,
1173:         null,
1174:         null,
1175:         { email, expiresAt },
1176:         now,
1177:       ),
1178:       outboxStatement(
1179:         environment.DB,
1180:         `invitation:created:outbox:${invitationId}`,
1181:         "invitation.created",
1182:         "invitation",
1183:         invitationId,
1184:         { email, expiresAt },
1185:         now,
1186:       ),
1187:     ]);
1188:   } catch (error) {
1189:     const conflictingInvitation = await createDb(environment.DB)
1190:       .select({ id: invitations.id })
1191:       .from(invitations)
1192:       .where(and(eq(invitations.email, email), inArray(invitations.status, ["pending", "claimed"])))
1193:       .get();
1194:     if (conflictingInvitation) throw new M1Error(409);
1195:     throw error;
1196:   }
1197: 
1198:   try {
1199:     await sendInvitationEmail(environment, { email, expiresAt, name, token });
1200:   } catch (error) {
1201:     await environment.DB.batch([
1202:       environment.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM audit_events WHERE id = ?").bind(
1203:         `invitation:created:${invitationId}`,
1204:       ),
1205:       environment.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM outbox_events WHERE dedupe_key = ?").bind(
1206:         `invitation:created:outbox:${invitationId}`,
1207:       ),
1208:       environment.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'pending'").bind(
1209:         invitationId,
1210:       ),
1211:     ]);
1212:     throw error;
1213:   }
1214:   return { email, expiresAt, id: invitationId, token };
1215: }

1219:   const invitation = await readInvitation(environment.DB, await sha256Base64Url(token));
1220:   if (!invitation) throw new M1Error(404);
1221:   const now = Date.now();
1222:   if (
1223:     (invitation.status === "pending" || invitation.status === "claimed") &&
1224:     invitation.expires_at <= now
1225:   ) {
1226:     await expireInvitation(environment.DB, invitation, now);

1234:   return {
1235:     email: invitation.email,
1236:     expiresAt: invitation.expires_at,
1237:     name: invitation.name,
1238:     status: invitation.status,
1239:   };

1242: async function claimInvitationWithAuth(
1243:   environment: AuthEnvironment,
1244:   auth: AuthInstance,
1245:   token: string,
1246:   body: InvitationAcceptBody,
1247:   request: Request,
1248: ) {
1249:   await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "invitation-accept", 30, 60);
1250:   const invitation = await readInvitation(environment.DB, await sha256Base64Url(token));
1251:   if (!invitation) throw new M1Error(404);
1252:   const now = Date.now();
1253:   const suppliedEmail = body.email ? normalizeEmail(body.email) : invitation.email;
1254:   if (suppliedEmail !== invitation.email) throw new M1Error(400);
1255:   const context = await auth.$context;
1256:   if (
1257:     body.password.length < context.password.config.minPasswordLength ||
1258:     body.password.length > context.password.config.maxPasswordLength
1259:   ) {
1260:     throw new M1Error(400);
1261:   }
1262: 
1263:   let current = invitation;
1264:   if (current.status === "pending") {
1265:     if (current.expires_at <= now) {
1266:       await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, now);
1267:       throw new M1Error(404);
1268:     }
1269:     const claimed = await environment.DB.prepare(
1270:       `UPDATE invitations
1271:             SET status = 'claimed', claimed_at = ?, updated_at = ?
1272:           WHERE id = ? AND status = 'pending' AND expires_at > ?
1273:         RETURNING id, token_hash, email, name, status, expires_at,
1274:                   invited_by_principal_id, claimed_user_id, claimed_principal_id,
1275:                   system_role_keys, claimed_at`,
1276:     )
1277:       .bind(now, now, current.id, now)
1278:       .first<Invitation>();
1279:     current = claimed ?? (await readInvitation(environment.DB, current.token_hash)) ?? current;
1280:   }
1281:   if (current.status === "pending" || current.status === "revoked") {
1282:     throw new M1Error(409);
1283:   }
1284:   if (current.status === "expired") {
1285:     await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, now);
1286:     throw new M1Error(409);
1287:   }
1288:   if (current.expires_at <= now) {
1289:     await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, now);
1290:     throw new M1Error(409);
1291:   }
1292:   if (current.status === "completed") throw new M1Error(409);
1293: 
1294:   const existingUser = await createDb(environment.DB)
1295:     .select({ id: user.id })
1296:     .from(user)
1297:     .where(eq(user.email, current.email))
1298:     .get();
1299:   const existingMapping = existingUser
1300:     ? await readHumanMapping(environment.DB, existingUser.id)
1301:     : undefined;
1302:   const hasActiveMapping =
1303:     existingMapping?.principal_status === "active" &&
1304:     existingMapping.human_status === "active" &&
1305:     existingMapping.disabled === 0;
1306:   const managedUser = await ensureControlledUser(
1307:     auth,
1308:     current.email,
1309:     normalizeName(body.name, current.name ?? current.email),
1310:     body.password,
1311:     current.claimed_user_id,
1312:     Boolean(current.claimed_user_id) || !hasActiveMapping,
1313:     current.claimed_at,
1314:   );
1315:   const marked = await environment.DB.prepare(
1316:     `UPDATE invitations
1317:           SET claimed_user_id = ?, updated_at = ?
1318:         WHERE id = ? AND status = 'claimed'
1319:           AND (claimed_user_id IS NULL OR claimed_user_id = ?)
1320:         RETURNING claimed_user_id`,
1321:   )
1322:     .bind(managedUser.id, Date.now(), current.id, managedUser.id)
1323:     .first<{ claimed_user_id: string }>();
1324:   if (!marked) {
1325:     const racedInvitation = await readInvitation(environment.DB, current.token_hash);
1326:     if (!racedInvitation || racedInvitation.claimed_user_id !== managedUser.id)
1327:       throw new M1Error(409);
1328:     current = racedInvitation;
1329:   } else {
1330:     current = (await readInvitation(environment.DB, current.token_hash)) ?? current;
1331:   }
1332:   if (current.status !== "claimed") throw new M1Error(409);
1333: 
1334:   const roleKeys = await validateRoleKeys(
1335:     environment.DB,
1336:     roleKeysFromStorage(current.system_role_keys),
1337:   );
1338:   await sendVerificationEmail(auth, managedUser);
1339:   const principalId = await ensureHumanPrincipal(environment.DB, managedUser.id, Date.now(), true);
1340:   const eventId = `invitation:completed:${current.id}`;
1341:   const completedAt = Date.now();
1342:   const statements = [
1343:     environment.DB.prepare(
1344:       `UPDATE invitations
1345:           SET status = 'completed', claimed_principal_id = ?, completed_at = ?, updated_at = ?
1346:           WHERE id = ? AND status = 'claimed' AND claimed_user_id = ?
1347:             AND expires_at > ?
1348:         RETURNING id`,
1349:     ).bind(principalId, completedAt, completedAt, current.id, managedUser.id, completedAt),
1350:     ...roleKeys.map((roleKey) =>
1351:       grantInvitationRoleStatement(
1352:         environment.DB,
1353:         current.id,
1354:         managedUser.id,
1355:         principalId,
1356:         roleKey,
1357:         current.invited_by_principal_id,
1358:         completedAt,
1359:       ),
1360:     ),
1361:     auditStatementWhen(
1362:       environment.DB,
1363:       eventId,
1364:       "invitation.completed",
1365:       current.invited_by_principal_id,
1366:       principalId,
1367:       managedUser.id,
1368:       { email: current.email },
1369:       completedAt,
1370:       "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'completed' AND claimed_user_id = ?",
1371:       [current.id, managedUser.id],
1372:     ),
1373:     outboxStatementWhen(
1374:       environment.DB,
1375:       `invitation:completed:outbox:${current.id}`,
1376:       "invitation.completed",
1377:       "invitation",
1378:       current.id,
1379:       { principalId, userId: managedUser.id },
1380:       completedAt,
1381:       "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'completed' AND claimed_user_id = ?",
1382:       [current.id, managedUser.id],
1383:     ),
1384:   ];
1385:   const results = await environment.DB.batch(statements);
1386:   const completionResult = results[0];
1387:   if (!completionResult?.results.length) {
1388:     await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, completedAt, true);
1389:     throw new M1Error(409);
1390:   }
1391:   return {
1392:     email: managedUser.email,
1393:     principalId,
1394:     status: "accepted" as const,
1395:     userId: managedUser.id,
1396:   };
1397: }

1418:   identifier: string,

1422:   const invitation = await resolveInvitationForRevoke(environment.DB, identifier);
1423:   if (!invitation) throw new M1Error(404);

1425:   const results = await environment.DB.batch([
1426:     environment.DB.prepare(
1427:       `UPDATE invitations
1428:             SET status = 'revoked', revoked_at = ?, updated_at = ?
1429:            WHERE id = ? AND status = 'pending'
1430:            RETURNING id`,

1432:     auditStatementWhen(
1433:       environment.DB,
1434:       `invitation:revoked:${invitation.id}`,
1435:       "invitation.revoked",
1436:       actor.principalId,
1437:       null,
1438:       null,
1439:       { invitationId: invitation.id },
1440:       now,
1441:       "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'revoked' AND revoked_at = ?",
1442:       [invitation.id, now],
1443:     ),
1444:     outboxStatementWhen(
1445:       environment.DB,
1446:       `invitation:revoked:outbox:${invitation.id}`,
1447:       "invitation.revoked",
1448:       "invitation",
1449:       invitation.id,
1450:       {},
1451:       now,
1452:       "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'revoked' AND revoked_at = ?",
1453:       [invitation.id, now],
1454:     ),
1455:   ]);
1456:   if (!results[0]?.results.length) {
1457:     const current = await resolveInvitationForRevoke(environment.DB, identifier);

1459:   }
1460:   return { id: invitation.id, status: "revoked" as const };

1: # Shui Roadmap
2: 
3: Last updated: 2026-08-14
4: 
5: ## Goal
6: 
7: Shui is a central identity platform that manages who can use each Application and which roles they have there. It communicates that state to Applications through OIDC/OAuth 2.1 and outbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning.
8: 
9: ```text
10: Identity Platform
11: ├── Principals
12: │   ├── Users
13: │   └── Service Accounts
14: ├── Teams
15: ├── System Roles
16: └── Applications
17:     ├── OAuth Resources
18:     ├── OIDC Clients
19:     ├── Assignments
20:     ├── Application Roles
21:     ├── Role Grants
22:     └── Provisioning
23: ```
24: 
25: ## Scope
26: 
27: ### Included
28: 
29: - Better Auth based human authentication and sessions
30: - OAuth 2.1 Provider with OIDC compatibility
31: - First-run setup that creates exactly one initial `root` User
32: - Invite-only User registration after setup
33: - Human Users and non-human Service Accounts
34: - Service Account credentials using the OAuth `client_credentials` grant
35: - User and Team ownership for Applications and Service Accounts
36: - System Roles for operating Shui
37: - Flat Teams containing Users
38: - Application Assignments independent from Application Roles
39: - Direct User and Service Account Application Role grants
40: - Team Application Role grants inherited by Team members
41: - Application-specific OIDC claims
42: - Outbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning with retries and reconciliation
43: - Responsive login, setup, invitation, consent, and administration UI
44: - Audit logging for security-sensitive and administrative operations
45: 
46: ### Not Included
47: 
48: - OAuth providers exposed by downstream Applications
49: - OAuth clients owned and managed inside downstream Applications
50: - Application-specific permissions such as `repo:write`
51: - Access tokens issued by downstream Applications
52: - Nested Teams or Team DAGs
53: - Deny roles or deny grants
54: - General-purpose policy language
55: - Inbound SCIM into Shui
56: 
57: ## Fixed Decisions
58: 
59: - Runtime and deployment: one Cloudflare Worker with a custom module entrypoint
60: - Web framework: TanStack Start with React 19
61: - API framework: Elysia mounted inside a TanStack Start server route under `/api/*`
62: - Elysia integration: dispatch standard `Request` objects through `app.fetch(request)` instead of exporting Elysia's experimental Cloudflare adapter directly
63: - Typed API client: Eden Treaty, using direct in-process calls during SSR and HTTP in the browser
64: - Database: Cloudflare D1 with Drizzle ORM
65: - Build and frontend delivery: Vite, `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, and Workers Static Assets
66: - UI: Kumo UI with Tailwind CSS v4
67: - Forms and server state: TanStack Form and TanStack Query
68: - API validation: Elysia `t` / TypeBox
69: - Formatting and linting: Vite+ with Oxlint, Oxfmt, and TypeScript strict mode
70: - Async provisioning: Cloudflare Queues with a dead-letter queue
71: - Authentication: Better Auth
72: - Provider: `@better-auth/oauth-provider`, not the legacy `oidcProvider`
73: - Better Auth version: pin all Better Auth packages to `1.7.0-rc.5`
74: - Teams remain separate from Principals; Principals are Users and Service Accounts
75: - Application Assignment and Application Role Grant are separate records
76: - Team Assignment is inherited by Team members
77: - Team Role Grants are inherited by Team members
78: - A Role Grant never creates an Assignment implicitly
79: - Roles are effective only while the subject has an effective Assignment
80: - Direct and Team-derived Role origins remain distinguishable
81: - Service Account credentials are OAuth Clients, not a second custom API-key system
82: - One Service Account can have multiple OAuth Client credentials for safe rotation
83: - Better Auth owns authentication protocol data; Shui owns authorization and provisioning data
84: - Better Auth Organization roles are not used as Shui System or Application Roles
85: - Better Auth SCIM plugin is not used because it provides inbound SCIM, while Shui needs outbound provisioning
86: - TanStack Start Server Functions do not contain domain business logic; domain reads and mutations go through Elysia services and routes

88: ## System Architecture
89: 
90: ```text
91: Browser
92:   │ HTTPS
93:   ▼
94: Single Cloudflare Worker
95:   ├── fetch
96:   │   └── TanStack Start
97:   │       ├── React 19 SSR and routing
98:   │       ├── Workers Static Assets
99:   │       └── /api/* -> Elysia app.fetch(request)
100:   │                    ├── Better Auth handler
101:   │                    │   ├── Email/password authentication
102:   │                    │   ├── Sessions
103:   │                    │   ├── OAuth 2.1 / OIDC Provider
104:   │                    │   └── JWT / JWKS
105:   │                    ├── Identity and authorization services
106:   │                    └── Audit and outbox writer
107:   ├── queue -> provisioning consumer
108:   └── scheduled -> outbox dispatch and reconciliation
109:        │
110:        ├── D1 via Drizzle
111:        ├── Cloudflare Queues
112:        └── Application SCIM endpoints
113: ```
114: 
115: Elysia's direct Cloudflare Worker adapter is currently experimental, so Shui does not export it as the Worker entrypoint. Elysia runs through its documented TanStack Start integration and receives requests through `app.fetch(request)`. This combined path must still be tested in the actual Workers runtime rather than only in Node.js. The custom Worker entrypoint delegates `fetch` to TanStack Start and also exposes `queue` and `scheduled` handlers.
116: 
117: ## Domain Semantics
118: 
119: ### Principals
120: 
121: `User` represents a human and maps one-to-one to a Better Auth User. `Service Account` represents a Bot, CI job, or backend process and never receives a fake email/password User.
122: 
123: Principal IDs are stable and never reused. Disabling a Principal immediately prevents new token issuance. Existing JWTs remain valid until expiration, so access-token lifetimes must stay short.
124: 
125: ### Teams
126: 
127: Teams contain Users only. Service Accounts cannot become Team members in the initial scope. Teams are flat and cannot contain other Teams.
128: 
129: Teams may own Applications and Service Accounts. Ownership identifies the responsible party but does not implicitly grant an Assignment, Application Role, or System Role.
130: 
131: ### System Roles
132: 
133: Initial built-in System Roles:
134: 
135: | Role | Purpose |
136: | --- | --- |
137: | `root` | Full control of Shui and recovery-critical operations |
138: | `user-admin` | Manage Users, invitations, Teams, and memberships |
139: | `application-admin` | Manage Applications, Assignments, Roles, OIDC Clients, and provisioning |
140: 
141: System Role definitions and permission mappings are code-defined initially. Grants are stored in D1. Application Roles remain dynamic and Application-specific.
142: 
143: The last active `root` User cannot be disabled, deleted, or stripped of `root`.
144: 
145: ### Applications
146: 
147: An Application is a service that trusts Shui. Each Application has:
148: 
149: - One OAuth Resource identifier used as the Access Token audience
150: - One or more OIDC/OAuth Clients
151: - Independent Assignments for Users, Service Accounts, and Teams
152: - Dynamic Application Roles
153: - Direct and Team Role Grants
154: - Optional outbound provisioning configuration
155: - An owner that is either a User or Team
156: 
157: Human-facing OIDC Clients and Service Account credentials are both OAuth Clients, but their purposes are recorded separately and validated differently.
158: 
159: ### Assignments
160: 
161: Assignment controls whether a subject may use an Application and whether it is included in provisioning.
162: 
163: ```text
164: effective User Assignment
165: = direct User Assignment
166:   OR active Assignment of any Team containing the User
167: 
168: effective Service Account Assignment
169: = direct Service Account Assignment
170: ```
171: 
172: The following states are intentionally different:
173: 
174: | State | Login/token issuance | Provisioning | Roles |
175: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
176: | Not assigned | Denied | Deprovisioned | Not effective |
177: | Assigned without Roles | Allowed | Active | Empty list |
178: | Assigned with Roles | Allowed | Active | Effective Role list |
179: 
180: ### Application Roles
181: 
182: Application Roles describe what a Principal is inside one Application. They do not define concrete permissions inside Shui or the downstream Application.
183: 
184: ```text
185: effective User Roles
186: = direct User Role Grants
187:   UNION Team Role Grants from all active Team memberships
188: 
189: effective Service Account Roles
190: = direct Service Account Role Grants
191: ```
192: 
193: Effective Role evaluation occurs only after an effective Assignment is confirmed. Duplicate Role keys are removed for claims, while all Direct and Team origins are retained for administration and audit responses.
194: 
195: Removing one origin does not remove a Role when another origin still grants it.
196: 
197: ### Service Account Credentials
198: 
199: Each Service Account credential is a confidential OAuth Client that supports `client_credentials` and is linked to exactly one Service Account and one Application Resource.
200: 
201: The OAuth Client's `client_id` and `client_secret` are the credential. The secret is displayed once and stored only in the secure form provided by Better Auth.
202: 
203: Credential rotation uses overlap rather than in-place secret rotation:
204: 
205: 1. Create a new OAuth Client credential.
206: 2. Link it to the same Service Account and Application Resource.
207: 3. Move the consumer to the new credential.
208: 4. Disable and later delete the old OAuth Client.
209: 
210: This avoids downtime because Better Auth's in-place rotation immediately invalidates the old secret.
211: 
212: ## OIDC And OAuth Contract
213: 
214: ### Flows
215: 
216: - Human login: Authorization Code Flow with PKCE S256
217: - Service Account: Client Credentials Grant
218: - Refresh Token Grant: disabled for the initial release
219: - Dynamic Client Registration: disabled
220: - Unauthenticated Client Registration: disabled
221: - JWT Access Tokens: required for downstream Applications
222: - Opaque Access Tokens: not accepted by downstream Applications
223: 
224: Refresh tokens remain disabled until Better Auth 1.7 is stable or D1 concurrency testing proves refresh-family rotation and invalidation safe.
225: 
226: ### Audience Rules
227: 
228: - Access Token `aud`: the target Application's OAuth Resource identifier
229: - ID Token `aud`: the authenticating OIDC `client_id`, as required by OIDC
230: - `iss`: Shui's canonical public issuer URL
231: - `azp` / `client_id`: the authenticated OAuth Client
232: 
233: Clients must be linked to allowed Resources. Managed Clients request exactly one Application Resource per flow. Tokens requesting no Resource, an unknown Resource, multiple Resources, or a Resource owned by another Application are rejected.
234: 
235: ### Claims
236: 
237: Standard OIDC claims are exposed according to scopes through ID Token and UserInfo behavior supported by Better Auth:
238: 
239: - `sub`
240: - `name`
241: - `email`
242: - `email_verified`
243: 
244: Shui-specific claims use a URI namespace based on the final issuer domain:
245: 
246: - `application_id`
247: - `principal_id`
248: - `principal_type`
249: - `roles`
250: - `teams`
251: - `authz_version`
252: 
253: Only data for the target Application is included. System Roles and Roles belonging to other Applications must never appear.
254: 
255: For human flows, `sub` identifies the User according to the Provider's subject policy. For `client_credentials`, `sub` identifies the OAuth Client credential. Applications use the namespaced `principal_id` claim when they need the stable Service Account identity across credential rotation.
256: 
257: Team claims contain only Teams relevant to the target Application. Claim keys and shape are versioned before the first production release.
258: 
259: ## Data Model Direction
260: 
261: Better Auth generated tables remain isolated as authentication infrastructure. Domain migrations reference Better Auth Users but do not modify generated tables manually unless required by a documented plugin extension.
262: 
263: Core Shui tables:
264: 
265: - `principals`
266: - `human_principals`
267: - `service_accounts`
268: - `teams`
269: - `team_memberships`
270: - `system_roles`
271: - `system_role_grants`
272: - `applications`
273: - `application_roles`
274: - Typed User, Service Account, and Team Assignment tables
275: - Typed User, Service Account, and Team Role Grant tables
276: - OAuth Resource and OAuth Client mapping tables
277: - Service Account OAuth Client credential mappings
278: - `invitations`
279: - `bootstrap_state`
280: - `provisioning_connections`
281: - `provisioning_resource_mappings`
282: - `outbox_events`
283: - `provisioning_deliveries`
284: - `audit_events`
285: 
286: Typed Assignment and Role Grant tables are preferred over nullable polymorphic foreign keys so D1 can enforce referential integrity for each subject type.
287: 
288: Domain records use soft deletion or disabling where identity, ownership, or audit references must remain stable. Relationship records such as membership, Assignment, and Role Grant may be physically deleted after an audit event and outbox event are written.
289: 
290: ## D1 Consistency Strategy
291: 
292: D1 is the source of truth. The implementation must not depend on long-running interactive transactions.
293: 
294: Use:
295: 
296: - Unique constraints for invariants
297: - Foreign keys for relational integrity
298: - Conditional updates for compare-and-swap behavior
299: - `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` for idempotency
300: - `D1Database.batch()` for atomic groups of prepared statements
301: - State machines when Better Auth writes and Shui domain writes cannot share one transaction
302: - Reconciliation jobs for cross-system convergence
303: 
304: Every administrative domain mutation writes its audit event and outbox event in the same D1 atomic batch.
305: 
306: Sending to Cloudflare Queues is not atomic with D1. An outbox dispatcher sends pending events to the Queue, and all consumers are idempotent. Duplicate and out-of-order delivery are expected.
307: 
308: ## Bootstrap And Invitations
309: 
310: ### Bootstrap
311: 
312: The first-run setup page is available only while `bootstrap_state` is incomplete. Production setup additionally requires a high-entropy `BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` stored as a Worker secret. The token is submitted in a POST body and never placed in a URL or log.
313: 
314: Bootstrap is an idempotent state machine:
315: 
316: ```text
317: uninitialized -> reserved -> user-created -> completed
318: ```
319: 
320: A singleton unique constraint and conditional writes ensure only one setup request can reserve initialization. Concurrent attempts lose safely. A failed reservation can be resumed only with the bootstrap secret; it is never automatically released to an anonymous caller.
321: 
322: Completion creates the Better Auth User, Human Principal, `root` grant, audit event, and required repair markers. After completion, setup endpoints return not found or redirect to sign-in.
323: 
324: ### Invitations
325: 
326: Public Better Auth sign-up is disabled. A custom invitation flow is the only post-bootstrap User creation path.
327: 
328: Invitation requirements:
329: 
330: - Cryptographically random token
331: - Only a token hash stored in D1
332: - Fixed normalized email address
333: - Explicit expiration
334: - Single-use atomic consumption
335: - Optional initial Team memberships and System Roles
336: - Revocation support
337: - Generic error responses that avoid account enumeration
338: - Idempotent recovery if Better Auth User creation succeeds before domain completion
339: 
340: ## Outbound Provisioning
341: 
342: Provisioning converges each Application toward Shui's desired state. Events are notifications to reconcile current state, not commands that must be applied blindly in event order.
343: 
344: ### Initial SCIM Coverage
345: 
346: - Create and update assigned Users
347: - Set `active: false` when a User loses effective Assignment or is disabled
348: - Create and update Teams as SCIM Groups where supported
349: - Synchronize Team membership
350: - Synchronize Application Role changes through per-Application mapping
351: - Synchronize Assignment changes
352: 
353: SCIM has no universal Application Role attribute. Each provisioning connection therefore defines one of these mappings:
354: 
355: - SCIM Group mapping
356: - Enterprise User extension mapping
357: - Application-specific schema extension
358: - No Role provisioning, leaving Roles available only through OIDC claims
359: 
360: Service Account provisioning is not part of the baseline SCIM User/Group implementation. It requires an explicit Application-specific mapping and is added only for Applications that support non-human SCIM identities.
361: 
362: ### Delivery Behavior
363: 
364: - Queue delivery is treated as at least once
365: - Desired-state version suppresses stale work
366: - Successful external resource IDs are persisted
367: - `429` and transient `5xx` responses retry with bounded exponential backoff
368: - Permanent `4xx` responses become operator-visible failures
369: - Exhausted retries go to a dead-letter queue
370: - Scheduled full reconciliation repairs missed or manually changed state
371: - Provisioning can be paused per Application
372: - Operators can retry or resynchronize an Application
373: 
374: Provisioning credentials are encrypted with AES-GCM using a versioned key stored outside D1 as a Worker secret or Secrets Store secret. Outbound requests require HTTPS, reject redirects, restrict destinations, cap response bodies, and redact credentials and personal data from logs.
375: 
376: ## UI Direction
377: 
378: The UI is a focused identity control plane rather than a generic admin template.
379: 
380: TanStack Start owns routing, SSR, and route-level loading. TanStack Query owns cached server state and mutations, while TanStack Form owns form state. Eden Treaty calls Elysia directly during SSR and over HTTP in the browser. Kumo UI provides accessible, source-tested primitives and semantic tokens, while Shui keeps its own page composition and brand treatment rather than using a generic dashboard template.

646: | D1 has limited transaction patterns and per-database serial throughput | Atomic batches, indexed short queries, no long transactions, production-like load tests |

648: | JWT Role changes are not instant | Short lifetimes, `authz_version`, optional live validation for high-risk Applications |

651: | First public deployment can be claimed before the owner arrives | Required Worker-secret bootstrap token and atomic singleton reservation |

224: async function consumeRateLimit(
225:   database: D1Database,
226:   key: string,
227:   rule: { max: number; window: number },
228: ) {
229:   const now = Date.now();
230:   const windowMilliseconds = rule.window * 1000;
231:   const bucket = await database
232:     .prepare(
233:       `INSERT INTO rate_limit_buckets
234:         (bucket_key, window_started_at, count, updated_at)
235:        VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?)
236:        ON CONFLICT(bucket_key) DO UPDATE SET
237:          count = CASE
238:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN 1
239:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.count + 1
240:          END,
241:          window_started_at = CASE
242:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN ?
243:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at
244:          END,
245:          updated_at = ?
246:        RETURNING count, window_started_at`,
247:     )
248:     .bind(key, now, now, windowMilliseconds, now, windowMilliseconds, now, now, now)
249:     .first<{ count: number; window_started_at: number }>();
250: 
251:   if (!bucket) return { allowed: false, retryAfter: rule.window };
252: 
253:   if (bucket.count === 1) {
254:     const db = createDb(database);
255:     await db
256:       .delete(rateLimitBuckets)
257:       .where(lt(rateLimitBuckets.updatedAt, now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000))
258:       .run();
259:   }
260: 
261:   const retryAfter = Math.max(
262:     0,
263:     Math.ceil((bucket.window_started_at + windowMilliseconds - now) / 1000),
264:   );
265: 
266:   return {
267:     allowed: bucket.count <= rule.max,
268:     retryAfter,
269:   };
270: }

428:         eq(principals.type, "human"),
429:         eq(principals.status, "active"),
430:       ),
431:     )
432:     .get();
433:   if (!principal || principal.userId !== session.user.id) throw new M1Error(401);

435:   const roleRows = await db
436:     .select({ key: systemRoles.key })
437:     .from(systemRoleGrants)

439:     .where(
440:       and(
441:         eq(systemRoleGrants.principalId, principal.principalId),
442:         isNull(systemRoleGrants.revokedAt),
443:       ),
444:     )
445:     .all();
446: 
447:   return {
448:     principalId: principal.principalId,
449:     roleKeys: new Set(roleRows.map((row) => row.key)),

465: async function ensureControlledUser(
466:   auth: AuthInstance,
467:   email: string,
468:   name: string,
469:   password: string,
470:   existingUserId?: string | null,
471:   allowExistingCredential = false,
472:   existingSince?: number | null,
473: ): Promise<ManagedUser> {
474:   const context = await auth.$context;
475:   let user = existingUserId ? await context.internalAdapter.findUserById(existingUserId) : null;
476: 
477:   if (!user) {
478:     const existing = await context.internalAdapter.findUserByEmail(email, {
479:       includeAccounts: true,
480:     });
481:     user = existing?.user ?? null;
482:     if (
483:       user &&
484:       !allowExistingCredential &&
485:       existing?.accounts.some((account) => account.providerId === "credential")
486:     ) {
487:       const createdAt = new Date(user.createdAt).getTime();
488:       if (!existingSince || createdAt < existingSince) throw new M1Error(409);
489:     }
490:   }
491:   if (user && normalizeEmail(user.email) !== email) throw new M1Error(409);
492: 
493:   if (!user) {
494:     const passwordHash = await context.password.hash(password);
495:     try {
496:       user = await context.internalAdapter.createUser(
497:         { email, emailVerified: false, name },
498:         { method: "email-password" },
499:       );
500:     } catch {
501:       user =
502:         (await context.internalAdapter.findUserByEmail(email, { includeAccounts: true }))?.user ??
503:         null;
504:       if (!user) throw new M1Error(500);
505:     }
506: 
507:     try {
508:       await context.internalAdapter.linkAccount({
509:         accountId: user.id,
510:         issuer: createLocalAccountIssuer("credential"),
511:         password: passwordHash,
512:         providerId: "credential",
513:         userId: user.id,
514:       });
515:     } catch {
516:       if (!(await context.internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount(user.id))) throw new M1Error(500);
517:     }
518:   } else {
519:     const credential = await context.internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount(user.id);
520:     if (!credential) {
521:       const passwordHash = await context.password.hash(password);
522:       try {
523:         await context.internalAdapter.linkAccount({
524:           accountId: user.id,
525:           issuer: createLocalAccountIssuer("credential"),
526:           password: passwordHash,
527:           providerId: "credential",
528:           userId: user.id,
529:         });
530:       } catch {
531:         if (!(await context.internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount(user.id))) throw new M1Error(500);
532:       }
533:     } else if (allowExistingCredential) {
534:       const passwordHash = await context.password.hash(password);
535:       await context.internalAdapter.updatePassword(user.id, passwordHash);
536:     }
537:   }
538: 
539:   return user as ManagedUser;
540: }

594: async function ensureHumanPrincipal(
595:   database: D1Database,
596:   userId: string,
597:   now: number,
598:   allowDisabled = false,
599: ) {
600:   const principalId = principalIdForUser(userId);
601:   const existingMapping = await readHumanMapping(database, userId);
602:   if (existingMapping && existingMapping.id !== principalId) throw new M1Error(409);
603:   if (
604:     existingMapping &&
605:     (existingMapping.type !== "human" ||
606:       (!allowDisabled &&
607:         (existingMapping.principal_status !== "active" ||
608:           existingMapping.human_status !== "active" ||
609:           existingMapping.disabled !== 0)))
610:   ) {
611:     throw new M1Error(409);
612:   }
613: 
614:   const existingPrincipal = await createDb(database)
615:     .select({ id: principals.id, type: principals.type, status: principals.status })
616:     .from(principals)
617:     .where(eq(principals.id, principalId))
618:     .get();
619:   if (
620:     existingPrincipal &&
621:     (existingPrincipal.type !== "human" ||
622:       (!allowDisabled && existingPrincipal.status !== "active"))
623:   ) {
624:     throw new M1Error(409);
625:   }
626: 
627:   const db = createDb(database);
628:   await db.batch([
629:     db
630:       .insert(principals)
631:       .values({
632:         id: principalId,
633:         type: "human",
634:         status: "active",
635:         disabledAt: null,
636:         createdAt: now,
637:         updatedAt: now,
638:       })
639:       .onConflictDoUpdate({
640:         target: principals.id,
641:         set: { disabledAt: null, status: "active", updatedAt: now },
642:       }),
643:     db
644:       .insert(humanPrincipals)
645:       .values({
646:         principalId,
647:         userId,
648:         status: "active",
649:         disabled: false,
650:         disabledAt: null,
651:         createdAt: now,
652:         updatedAt: now,
653:       })
654:       .onConflictDoUpdate({
655:         target: humanPrincipals.principalId,
656:         set: { disabled: false, disabledAt: null, status: "active", userId, updatedAt: now },
657:       }),
658:   ]);
659: 
660:   const mapping = await readHumanMapping(database, userId);
661:   if (
662:     !mapping ||
663:     mapping.id !== principalId ||
664:     mapping.principal_status !== "active" ||
665:     mapping.human_status !== "active" ||
666:     mapping.disabled !== 0
667:   ) {
668:     throw new M1Error(500);
669:   }
670: 
671:   return principalId;

765: async function completeBootstrapDomain(
766:   database: D1Database,
767:   state: BootstrapState,
768:   user: ManagedUser,
769:   principalId: string,
770:   now: number,
771: ) {
772:   const existingRoot = await createDb(database)
773:     .select({ principalId: systemRoleGrants.principalId })
774:     .from(systemRoleGrants)
775:     .innerJoin(systemRoles, eq(systemRoles.id, systemRoleGrants.roleId))
776:     .innerJoin(principals, eq(principals.id, systemRoleGrants.principalId))
777:     .innerJoin(humanPrincipals, eq(humanPrincipals.principalId, principals.id))
778:     .where(
779:       and(
780:         eq(systemRoles.key, "root"),
781:         isNull(systemRoleGrants.revokedAt),
782:         eq(principals.type, "human"),
783:         eq(principals.status, "active"),
784:         eq(humanPrincipals.status, "active"),
785:         eq(humanPrincipals.disabled, false),
786:       ),
787:     )
788:     .get();
789:   if (existingRoot && existingRoot.principalId !== principalId) throw new M1Error(409);
790: 
791:   const email = state.email ?? normalizeEmail(user.email);
792:   const eventId = `bootstrap:completed:${state.reservation_id ?? principalId}`;
793:   const results = await database.batch([
794:     database
795:       .prepare(
796:         `UPDATE bootstrap_state
797:             SET status = 'completed', principal_id = ?, completed_at = ?, updated_at = ?
798:           WHERE id = 1
799:             AND status IN ('reserved', 'user-created')
800:             AND reservation_id = ?
801:             AND email = ?
802:             AND user_id = ?
803:           RETURNING id`,
804:       )
805:       .bind(principalId, now, now, state.reservation_id, email, user.id),
806:     grantBootstrapRoleStatement(database, state.reservation_id ?? "", user.id, principalId, now),
807:     auditStatementWhen(
808:       database,
809:       eventId,
810:       "bootstrap.completed",
811:       null,
812:       principalId,
813:       user.id,
814:       { email },
815:       now,
816:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'completed' AND reservation_id = ? AND user_id = ?",
817:       [state.reservation_id, user.id],
818:     ),
819:     outboxStatementWhen(
820:       database,
821:       `bootstrap:completed:outbox:${state.reservation_id ?? principalId}`,
822:       "bootstrap.completed",
823:       "bootstrap",
824:       "1",
825:       { principalId, userId: user.id },
826:       now,
827:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'completed' AND reservation_id = ? AND user_id = ?",
828:       [state.reservation_id, user.id],
829:     ),
830:   ]);
831:   if (!results[0]?.results.length) throw new M1Error(409);
832: }

834: async function reserveBootstrap(
835:   environment: AuthEnvironment,
836:   body: BootstrapTokenBody,
837:   request: Request,
838: ) {
839:   await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "bootstrap-reserve", 50, 60);
840:   await requireBootstrapToken(environment, body);
841:   const state = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
842:   if (state.status === "completed") throw new M1Error(404);
843:   if (state.status !== "uninitialized") {
844:     if (!state.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(500);
845:     return { reservationId: state.reservation_id, status: state.status };
846:   }
847: 
848:   const reservationId = crypto.randomUUID();
849:   const now = Date.now();
850:   const results = await environment.DB.batch([
851:     environment.DB.prepare(
852:       `UPDATE bootstrap_state
853:               SET status = 'reserved', reservation_id = ?, reserved_at = ?, updated_at = ?
854:             WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'uninitialized'
855:             RETURNING reservation_id, status`,
856:     ).bind(reservationId, now, now),
857:     auditStatementWhen(
858:       environment.DB,
859:       `bootstrap:reserved:${reservationId}`,
860:       "bootstrap.reserved",
861:       null,
862:       null,
863:       null,
864:       {},
865:       now,
866:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'reserved' AND reservation_id = ? AND reserved_at = ?",
867:       [reservationId, now],
868:     ),
869:     outboxStatementWhen(
870:       environment.DB,
871:       `bootstrap:reserved:outbox:${reservationId}`,
872:       "bootstrap.reserved",
873:       "bootstrap",
874:       "1",
875:       { reservationId },
876:       now,
877:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'reserved' AND reservation_id = ? AND reserved_at = ?",
878:       [reservationId, now],
879:     ),
880:   ]);
881:   const reserved = results[0]?.results[0] as
882:     | { reservation_id: string; status: BootstrapStatus }
883:     | undefined;
884: 
885:   if (!reserved) {
886:     const racedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
887:     if (racedState.status === "completed" || !racedState.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(409);
888:     return { reservationId: racedState.reservation_id, status: racedState.status };
889:   }
890: 
891:   return { reservationId, status: reserved.status };
892: }

894: async function completeBootstrap(
895:   environment: AuthEnvironment,
896:   auth: AuthInstance,
897:   body: BootstrapCompleteBody,
898:   request: Request,
899: ) {
900:   await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "bootstrap-complete", 50, 60);
901:   await requireBootstrapToken(environment, body);
902:   const state = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
903:   if (state.status === "completed") {
904:     if (state.email && normalizeEmail(body.email) !== state.email) throw new M1Error(409);
905:     return { status: state.status, userId: state.user_id };
906:   }
907:   if (state.status === "uninitialized" || !state.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(409);
908:   if (body.reservationId && body.reservationId !== state.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(409);
909: 
910:   const email = normalizeEmail(body.email);
911:   if (state.email && state.email !== email) throw new M1Error(409);
912: 
913:   const context = await auth.$context;
914:   if (
915:     body.password.length < context.password.config.minPasswordLength ||
916:     body.password.length > context.password.config.maxPasswordLength
917:   ) {
918:     throw new M1Error(400);
919:   }
920: 
921:   if (!state.email) {
922:     const claimedEmail = await environment.DB.prepare(
923:       `UPDATE bootstrap_state
924:             SET email = ?, updated_at = ?
925:           WHERE id = 1
926:             AND status = 'reserved'
927:             AND reservation_id = ?
928:             AND (email IS NULL OR email = ?)
929:           RETURNING email`,
930:     )
931:       .bind(email, Date.now(), state.reservation_id, email)
932:       .first<{ email: string }>();
933:     if (!claimedEmail) {
934:       const racedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
935:       if (racedState.email !== email) throw new M1Error(409);
936:     }
937:   }
938: 
939:   const user = await ensureControlledUser(
940:     auth,
941:     email,
942:     normalizeName(body.name, email),
943:     body.password,
944:     state.user_id,
945:     false,
946:     state.reserved_at,
947:   );
948:   const marked = await environment.DB.prepare(
949:     `UPDATE bootstrap_state
950:           SET status = 'user-created', user_id = ?, user_created_at = COALESCE(user_created_at, ?), updated_at = ?
951:         WHERE id = 1
952:           AND status IN ('reserved', 'user-created')
953:           AND reservation_id = ?
954:           AND email = ?
955:           AND (user_id IS NULL OR user_id = ?)
956:         RETURNING user_id`,
957:   )
958:     .bind(user.id, Date.now(), Date.now(), state.reservation_id, email, user.id)
959:     .first<{ user_id: string }>();
960:   if (!marked) {
961:     const racedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
962:     if (racedState.user_id !== user.id) throw new M1Error(409);
963:   }
964: 
965:   const markedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
966:   await sendVerificationEmail(auth, user);
967:   const principalId = await ensureHumanPrincipal(environment.DB, user.id, Date.now());
968:   await completeBootstrapDomain(environment.DB, markedState, user, principalId, Date.now());
969: 
970:   return { principalId, status: "completed" as const, userId: user.id };
971: }

1018:     database
1019:       .prepare(
1020:         `UPDATE human_principals

1044:       .prepare(

1049:                 i.claimed_user_id, ?, ?

1054:         `invitation:expired:${invitation.id}`,
